s1.syndrome_frame: Facial asymmetry in a neonate with a cerebellopontine angle mass and hearing loss
salient_findings: Enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal
Profound hearing loss in the left ear
key_facts: 4-week-old male patient
Left facial asymmetry observed during crying
Passed infant hearing screening
MRI showed an enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal
Follow-up MRI showed considerable growth of the mass
ABR testing demonstrated profound hearing loss in the left ear
Histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity
Biphasic lesion composed of vascular nodules among spindle cells
Ki-67 labeling index: 5% to 10%
CD34 and CD31: Positive for endothelial cells

shortlist: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (KHE) of the internal auditory canal

shortlist.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (KHE) of the internal auditory canal
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the biphasic vascular lesion with spindle cells and glomeruloid-like architecture described in the histopathological examination

shortlist.label: Congenital Hemangioblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the enhancing mass in the cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal, although less likely given the histopathological features

shortlist.label: Epithelioid Hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the vascular lesion and endothelial cell markers, but less typical for the location and age of the patient

shortlist.label: Infantile hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Common in infants, but the histopathological features and location are not typical for this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Hemangioblastoma of the cerebellopontine angle
shortlist.why_kept: Although a possibility, the histopathological features and age of the patient make it less likely than KHE

s4.champion: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (KHE) of the internal auditory canal

raw.champion: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (KHE) of the internal auditory canal
raw.rationale: The patient's age, location of the mass, and histopathological findings, including a biphasic lesion with vascular nodules and spindle cells, are consistent with KHE. The Ki-67 labeling index and positive CD34 and CD31 staining also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Congenital Hemangioblastoma
rejected.why: Hemangioblastomas typically have a higher mitotic activity and are more commonly associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease

rejected.label: Epithelioid Hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: This tumor type usually presents with more epithelioid morphology and higher nuclear grade, which is not described in the histopathological examination

rejected.label: Infantile hemangioma
rejected.why: Infantile hemangiomas typically regress over time and do not usually present with such aggressive growth or profound hearing loss

rejected.label: Hemangioblastoma of the cerebellopontine angle
rejected.why: The histopathological description does not match the typical features of hemangioblastoma, which includes rich vascularity and stromal cells
